author: mattcheramie
body:
## Summary

This is the follow-up to the Mueller-Müller chunk-boundary fix (#311), which flagged a residual ~4% clean-signal C4FM dibit error rate as a "timing-loop quality" follow-up. Investigating it showed the residual was **a harness artifact, not a demod fault** — and uncovered a real coverage gap.

**Root cause.** The #275 reproduction harness filled its warmup / idle / trailer dibits with a periodic `0,1,2,3` ramp. The Mueller-Müller symbol-timing detector is data-pattern dependent: measuring its S-curve showed the periodic filler biased the detector's equilibrium ~2 samples off the eye centre. So the harness measured a ~4% residual error and the C4FM control channel only locked when the signal happened to start exactly phase-aligned — which only synthetic test signals are. On a *random* dibit stream the S-curve crosses zero exactly at the eye centre: **the Mueller-Müller loop is correct.**

**Fix.** Real P25 control-channel dibits are effectively random (back-to-back trellis-coded TSBKs). `buildHarnessDibits` now fills warmup / idle / trailer with pseudo-random dibits (fixed seed, reproducible). With it:
- the clean-signal C4FM dibit error rate drops from 0.042 to **0.000**;
- the C4FM control channel locks at **every** symbol-timing phase (was 4/10).

**New coverage.** `TestHarnessC4FMTimingPhaseAcquisition` feeds the C4FM control channel at every symbol-timing phase offset and asserts a lock. The harness fed only phase-aligned signals before, so symbol-clock acquisition from an arbitrary phase — what every real RTL-SDR capture presents — was never exercised. `runHarness` is refactored over a new `runHarnessPhase(mode, imp, skip)` that applies the phase offset.

This is a **test-only change** — no production code is touched, because the investigation confirmed the demod is correct.

## Test plan

- [x] Investigated via the Mueller-Müller TED S-curve: periodic filler biases the zero to ~+2.2 samples; random filler crosses zero at the eye centre
- [x] `TestHarnessC4FMTimingPhaseAcquisition` — C4FM locks at all 10 symbol-timing phases (was 4/10 with the periodic filler)
- [x] `TestHarnessC4FMDibitErrorRate` — clean DER 0.000 (was 0.042); threshold tightened to 0.02
- [x] All existing harness tests pass (clean lock, carrier offset, chunk boundary, CQPSK gain/equalizer/chunk)
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, full `go test ./...` — clean
- [x] `-race` on the receiver package, and `make integration-cc` — green

Resolves the residual flagged in #311; confirms the C4FM symbol-timing recovery is sound.

author: octalide
body:
## Summary

PR 4 of the application-flow pass. Adds an explicit **import** flow — copy raw files from any source folder into the library directory. The library still indexes in place; this layers a copy step on top.

### Import engine — `src/library/import.c`

`ap_import_run` recursively scans a source folder for raws and copies each into `<lib_root>/<subdir>/` (default `raw`). **Source files are never modified**; the copy carries the source's mtime.

Per-library settings persist in the library db's `settings` table:
- **destination subdir**
- **naming** — keep the original filename, or rename by a pattern
- **rename pattern** — tokens `{ORIG} {YYYY} {MM} {DD} {HH} {MIN} {SEC} {SEQ}`; date/time from the raw's EXIF capture time (LibRaw), falling back to the source mtime; `{SEQ}` is a 4-digit per-import counter
- **collision** — skip / overwrite / auto-suffix (overwrite guards against copying a file onto itself)

### Supporting changes

- `ap_raw_capture_time` — reads a raw's EXIF timestamp via a metadata-only LibRaw open (no pixel decode).
- `ap_raw_is_raw_path` — the raw-extension check moves to `io/raw` as the single source of truth; `library.c`'s scanner delegates to it (its duplicate list is removed).
- `ap_library_setting_get` / `_set` — generic per-library key/value settings.

### UI

**File > Import** opens a modal: a native folder picker (the NFDe dialog from #171) for the source, the four settings edited in place and persisted on import, and an Import button. After copying, the library is reopened so the new photos are indexed.

## Test plan (needs interactive verification)

- [ ] Rename-by-pattern produces names from the tokens; `{YYYY}{MM}{DD}` reflects EXIF capture date.
- [ ] Collision: skip leaves existing files; auto-suffix appends `_1`; overwrite replaces.

Previously, if `runFixture` threw on a fixture and the developer ran with `--update-baseline`, `saveBaseline` would persist a `score: 0` entry for that fixture. A subsequent judge score of 8 would compute delta +8 and pass the gate — permanently muting that fixture from regression detection.

The runner already exits non-zero on infra errors, so refusing the baseline write is the simpler "harder-to-footgun" path the issue author called out as the preference.

## Changes
- `tests/evals/feature-evals.ts`: guard the `saveBaseline` call on `report.infraErrors.length === 0`; otherwise log an error explaining the skip

## What changed

- Added `hackerai-usage_cost` events with user, subscription, org, chat, endpoint, mode, model, token, and dollar-cost fields.

---
### Kimchi Summary
### What changed
Restores PostHog product analytics to the CLI by capturing key lifecycle events—`app_started`, `harness_launched`, `setup_completed`, `setup_aborted`, and `tool_configured`—using a persistent device ID. Events are only sent when telemetry is enabled, and the API key is injected at build time via CI.

### Why
Enables product usage insights while respecting the existing telemetry opt-out configuration.

### Key changes
- `src/posthog.ts` (added): Fire-and-forget HTTP capture to PostHog with default properties (`cli_version`, `os`, `arch` mapped to Go-compatible values); swallows errors and no-ops when `KIMCHI_POSTHOG_API_KEY` is unset.
- `src/posthog-device.ts` (added): `ensureDeviceId()` reads or generates a persisted UUID distinct ID; skips generation when telemetry is disabled.
- `src/cli.ts`: Tracks `app_started` on every invocation and `harness_launched` when a harness session begins; awaits pending PostHog flushes at exit to reduce truncated requests.
- `src/commands/setup.ts`: Sends `setup_aborted` (with step name), `tool_configured` (per selected tool), and `setup_completed` (with tool count and scope) during the setup wizard.
- `src/config.ts`: Adds `deviceId` field with read-time fallback to legacy `device_id`; adds `writeDeviceId()` which clears the legacy key.
- `.github/workflows/canary.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`: Expose `KIMCHI_POSTHOG_API_KEY` from `secrets.POSTHOG_API_KEY` to the binary build step.
- `src/setup-wizard/index.ts` and `state.ts`: Enriches the wizard result with `cancelledStep` and `selectedTools` for more specific analytics properties.

### Impact
- Dev builds without `KIMCHI_POSTHOG_API_KEY` silently skip analytics with no functional impact.
- Analytics requests are non-blocking (5-second timeout) and do not affect CLI performance or error handling.
- Fully additive; no breaking changes or migration steps required.

---
## Проблема

Игра не запускается дальше главного меню. На экране отображается меню (camp/tavern), внизу надпись "[AdMob Banner — Test Mode]", но **ни одна кнопка не реагирует** на нажатия. Сюжет, режим испытаний, настройки — всё мёртвое.

## Причина (Root Cause)

Комбинация из нескольких дефектов в системе монетизации:

### 1. Блокирующий CDN-скрипт в `<head>`
```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@nicedoc/capacitor-core@latest/dist/capacitor.js" ...>
```
- Пакет `@nicedoc/capacitor-core` — **неправильный** (должен быть `@capacitor/core`)
- Загружался **синхронно** в `<head>` — блокировал парсинг всей страницы
- При недоступности CDN — таймаут, при получении ответа — потенциально сломанный JS определяющий `window.Capacitor` некорректно

### 2. Отсутствие защиты в Monetization
- `_detectNative()` вызывала `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` без try-catch — если CDN-скрипт определил сломанный объект, бросалось исключение
- `showBanner()` проверяла только `!_isNative`, но не `!_admob` — при некорректном Capacitor можно было получить `TypeError: null.showBanner`
- `Monetization.initialize()` вызывалась в BOOT без `.catch()` — rejected Promise не обрабатывался

### 3. Эмулированный баннер перехватывал клики
- `z-index: 9999` + без `pointer-events: none` = баннер внизу экрана мог перехватывать тач-события на нижних кнопках camp UI

### 4. Отсутствие try-catch в BOOT
- Если `Monetization.initialize()` бросала синхронную ошибку, последующие вызовы (`TitleScreen.init()`, `Game.init()`) не выполнялись

## Исправления

| Файл | Что сделано |
|------|-------------|
| `index.html` | Удалён CDN-скрипт Capacitor, заменён на `window.Capacitor = null` stub |
| `js/monetization.js` | `_detectNative()`, `_detectPlatform()`, `_getAdMobPlugin()` обёрнуты в try-catch; `showBanner()`/`hideBanner()` проверяют `!_admob`; баннеру добавлен `pointer-events:none` |
| `js/core/state-machine.js` | `Monetization.initialize()` обёрнут в try-catch + `.catch()`; `Game.init()` обёрнут в try-catch |
| `js/core/game-loop.js` | Все вызовы `Monetization.*` обёрнуты в try-catch; `_afterTitleDismissed()` защищён |

## Проверка

После исправления поток:
1. ✅ `index.html` парсится мгновенно (нет блокирующего CDN)
2. ✅ `Monetization.initialize()` — `Capacitor = null` → `_isNative = false` → emulation mode → return
3. ✅ `Game.init()` выполняется полностью — кнопки привязываются
4. ✅ `UI.showCamp()` — camp overlay с кнопками отображается
5. ✅ Баннер отрисовывается внизу с `pointer-events:none` — не блокирует UI
6. ✅ Клик на "Испытания" → `showMapSelect()` → выбор биома → `startNewGame()`
7. ✅ Клик на "Сюжет" → `_showStoryCampaignMenu()` → новая/продолжение кампании

body:
## Summary

Task's \`env:\` block **does NOT propagate** from a parent task to a sub-task invoked via \`task:\` directive. PRs #181 and #182 both relied on this propagation and silently failed — parent task set \`BACKEND_BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY\` in its env block, but the sub-task \`test:e2e:agentic:stack:up\` (which actually runs \`docker compose up\`) didn't inherit it. Compose substituted \`\${BACKEND_BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY:-}\` to empty; backend booted with the \`web_search\` stub.

Confirmed by bisect with a diagnostic taskfile that echoed at each stage:

| Stage | Length | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1. shell sees dotenv var | 31 | ✅ |
| 2. \`sh:\` var captures via \`vars\` block | 31 | ✅ |
| 3. env block forwards in parent task shell | 31 | ✅ |
| 4. **sub-task inherits parent env block** | **0** | ❌ |
| 5. docker compose substitution | empty | ❌ |

## Fix

Move the env: setting to \`test:e2e:agentic:stack:up\` — the task that actually invokes \`docker compose up\`. The smoke6 task passes the host's BRAVE key to stack:up as a task **var** (\`BACKEND_BRAVE_KEY\`); stack:up reads that var into its own env block as \`BACKEND_BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY\`, which the compose substitution then sees.

Mock-LLM journey opt-in semantics preserved: tasks that call stack:up without passing \`BACKEND_BRAVE_KEY\` default it to empty → compose substitutes empty → framework registers the stub.

## Verified end-to-end with second diagnostic

\`\`\`
Parent: HOST_BRAVE_KEY length = 31
Sub:    BACKEND_BRAVE_KEY (task var) length = 31
Sub:    BACKEND_BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY (env) shell-visible: 31
Sub-shell substitution: BACKEND_BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY=BSAsBD...
\`\`\`

## Track record

Closes the silent-failure that smoke6-post181, smoke6-post182, smoke6-post182-take5 all hit (backend boot log: \`Registered web_search tool provider=stub\`). Three prior PRs (#181, #182, and this one) chased the same symptom; this one actually fixes the mechanism.

## Test plan

- [x] Bisect proved the gap (parent env doesn't propagate to sub-task)
- [x] Verified end-to-end with second diagnostic that mirrored the new wiring
- [ ] Re-run \`task ui:test:e2e:agentic:smoke6:run\` post-merge — expect \`provider=brave\` in backend boot log; chain converges in ~6 loops at ~\$0.30
- [ ] Spot-check \`task ui:test:e2e:agentic:research-mvp\` to confirm \`provider=stub\` (opt-out preserved)

author: frankhli843
body:
## Objective

Fix the Gemmaclaw/Jake compaction retry path that still had a hard 60s aggregate timeout after PR #215. In the live Jake trace, that cap could fire before slow Pi compaction finished, causing the visible user turn to fall back to pre-compaction state and surface the incomplete-turn warning instead of the refreshed answer.

## Change Summary

- Replaced the hardcoded `60_000` compaction retry aggregate timeout in `attempt.ts` with the configured compaction safety timeout.
- Kept the fallback bounded by the existing compaction safety window, defaulting to 900s.
- Updated the compaction retry helper comment so it describes the caller-configured safety timeout.
- Extended the attempt test harness to expose the compaction timeout resolver and retry wait mock.
- Added `attempt.compaction-retry-timeout.test.ts` to assert a configured `timeoutSeconds: 123` becomes a `123_000ms` retry wait.

## Non-Goals

- No changes to compaction execution itself.
- No unbounded waits.
- No model, prompt, benchmark, setup, or site behavior changes.
- No Jake-only config patch.

## Baseline Evidence

The interrupted `/iterate_gemma` investigation reconstructed the current failure from Jake logs and source state:

- Expected behavior: after forced compaction, the visible user turn waits for refreshed post-compaction context and returns a normal answer.
- Observed behavior: PR #215 removed one bad timeout path, but the visible turn could still hit `compaction retry aggregate timeout (60000ms)` and proceed with pre-compaction state.
- Code evidence: `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.ts` still defined `COMPACTION_RETRY_AGGREGATE_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` and passed it into `waitForCompactionRetryWithAggregateTimeout`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The compaction retry wait uses the configured compaction safety timeout, not a fixed 60s cap.
- Slow Pi/Jake compaction can continue for the configured window before fallback.
- Lost or stuck compaction retry resolution still falls back after a bounded safety timeout.
- Tests prove the configured timeout is passed to the retry wait path.

## Verification Map

- Requirement: remove premature 60s fallback.
  Code path: `runEmbeddedAttempt` in `attempt.ts`.
  Test: `attempt.compaction-retry-timeout.test.ts` asserts `aggregateTimeoutMs: 123_000`.

- Requirement: preserve bounded failure behavior.
  Code path: `waitForCompactionRetryWithAggregateTimeout` still receives a finite aggregate timeout from `resolveCompactionTimeoutMs`.
  Existing coverage: `compaction-retry-aggregate-timeout.test.ts` covers timeout and abort behavior.

- Requirement: avoid regressions in touched runtime paths.
  Checks run: targeted compaction tests plus `pnpm check:changed`.

## Consequence Check

Does this solve the original failure? Yes. The known premature fallback came from the remaining fixed `60_000ms` retry cap. This change removes that cap and uses the same configured compaction safety window used by the rest of the embedded run timeout handling.

Slow dependency behavior: slow-but-valid Pi compaction now has the configured safety window, default 900s, to complete instead of being cut off after one minute.

Partial or failing dependency behavior: if compaction retry resolution is lost or compaction remains in flight past the safety window, the existing timeout path still logs and falls back. This does not turn the wait into an unbounded hang.

Edge cases introduced: a genuinely stuck compaction can hold the session lane longer than before, up to the configured safety timeout. That is the intended tradeoff because the previous 60s bound dropped valid slow completions and left sessions near the context cliff.

## Diagrams

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant UserTurn as Visible user turn
  participant Attempt as runEmbeddedAttempt
  participant Compact as Compaction retry
  participant Timeout as Safety timeout

  UserTurn->>Attempt: Needs compaction retry
  Attempt->>Timeout: resolveCompactionTimeoutMs(config)
  Attempt->>Compact: waitForCompactionRetryWithAggregateTimeout(timeout)
  alt retry completes inside configured window
    Compact-->>Attempt: refreshed post-compaction state ready
    Attempt-->>UserTurn: continue visible answer
  else retry exceeds configured window
    Timeout-->>Attempt: bounded timeout
    Attempt-->>UserTurn: fallback with explicit warning path
  end
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Compaction retry needed] --> B[Resolve configured compaction safety timeout]
  B --> C[Wait for retry with configured aggregate timeout]
  C -->|Completes| D[Use refreshed post-compaction context]
  C -->|Times out| E[Log bounded timeout and fall back]
  D --> F[Visible reply resumes]
  E --> G[No indefinite lane hold]
```

## Checks Run

```bash
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 pnpm test src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.compaction-retry-timeout.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/compaction-retry-aggregate-timeout.test.ts && OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 pnpm check:changed
```

Results:

- Targeted compaction tests: 2 files passed, 8 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed, 17 test files passed, 237 tests passed.

body:
Wires the L0 reproducibility baseline into the multi-pass runner. Three new modules:

- `meshqu_runner/substrate_cache.py` — reads the 283-record corpus from E1's frozen archive at `procurement-decisions/results/runs/dry-run-7ddf7274-695f-4b1b-a335-b8ed006cc26d/`. Parses the archived `user_message` back into its structured envelope (`decision_type`, `fields`, `substrate_notes`) and cross-references `decision_traces.jsonl` for the `ocid → decision_id` mapping + E1 audit metadata. Pure disk read; no network calls.
- `meshqu_runner/context_levels/level_l0.py` — live L0 handler. Inherits the empty-addendum contract from the E2-001 stub. `install_live_l0()` implements the registry-replacement pattern so `default_main_handlers()` is left untouched.
- `scripts/compare_l0_to_e1.py` — L0-vs-E1 reproducibility comparator. Verdict-comparison table covering both MeshQu policy verdict and agent verdict; exits 0 on all-match, 1 otherwise.

## PR-body answers (per package contract)

### Where does the substrate cache read from?

`procurement-decisions/results/runs/dry-run-7ddf7274-695f-4b1b-a335-b8ed006cc26d/` — the E1 frozen archive. Specifically:

- `decision_traces.jsonl` for the `ocid → decision_id` mapping + E1 audit fields (verdicts, violations, integrity hash).
- `agent_outputs/<decision_id>.json` for the per-record `user_message` (the canonical-JSON envelope E1 sent to the agent at L0). Parsed back to `{decision_type, fields, substrate_notes}` — the shape `build_user_message` consumes.

E1 did NOT persist raw OCDS bytes; we reconstruct the substrate envelope from the *adapter output* E1 archived. This indirection is documented in `planning/decision_log.md` under the new E2-002 entry. Byte-for-byte reproducibility of the L0 prompt is verified on all 283 records (see test below).

### Did the 3-smoke-record L0-vs-E1 comparison pass?

The live comparator requires OpenAI + MeshQu credentials and runs as part of E2-007's smoke. This package wired the comparator and validated it against a stub run end-to-end. Stub-run output (deterministic; both stub agent and stub MeshQu emit `REVIEW`, which is the expected mismatch shape against the live E1 archive):

| OCID (last 12) | E1 MeshQu | L0 MeshQu | E1 Agent | L0 Agent | Match | Note                                           |
|----------------|-----------|-----------|----------|----------|-------|------------------------------------------------|
| f2735d803e4f   | DENY      | REVIEW    | REVIEW   | REVIEW   | no    | stub bundle (not a live reproducibility check) |
| 4b8ab05f7658   | ALLOW     | REVIEW    | REVIEW   | REVIEW   | no    | stub bundle (not a live reproducibility check) |
| 7db01e366670   | DENY      | REVIEW    | REVIEW   | REVIEW   | no    | stub bundle (not a live reproducibility check) |

The 3 default OCIDs selected (deterministic):

- `ocds-b5fd17-282a00c5-37ef-4eed-b308-f2735d803e4f` (decision_id `ca19e737-…`, worked-example £57M case, E1 MeshQu=DENY, violations=PROC-001-S53 + PROC-002-AUTHORITY + PROC-005-OPEN-TENDER)
- `ocds-b5fd17-001cf81b-5232-4d78-a0c7-4b8ab05f7658` (decision_id `7adc6b52-…`, first clean ALLOW, no violations)
- `ocds-b5fd17-0786919f-4875-42c3-99ac-7db01e366670` (decision_id `90c8d504-…`, first single-rule DENY, PROC-005-OPEN-TENDER only)

The stub run is not a real reproducibility check — the comparator marks each row with `"stub bundle (not a live reproducibility check)"` so a PR reader doesn't mistake the always-mismatch shape for a substrate-loading bug. The LIVE 3-record verdict table is E2-007's deliverable.

### If verdicts mismatched on ≥1 smoke record: name the record, name the divergence, suggest whether it's noise or a bug

N/A for the stub run — all rows mismatch by construction (stub always emits REVIEW; the comparator flags this with the stub note). The live invocation is gated on E2-007 per the package's separation of concerns (E2-002 ships the comparator, E2-007 runs it against live credentials).

If E2-007's live run produces a MeshQu-verdict mismatch on any record, that's a substrate-loading or hash-binding bug — investigate before proceeding. If only the agent verdict mismatches on ≤1 of 3 records, that's within the temp=0 reproducibility band (E1 P4 deferral). The comparator's exit code + table support this triage.

## Reproducibility strength

The package required byte-for-byte match on the worked-example OCID, accepting whitespace normalisation if needed. The actual implementation matches **all 283 records** with NO normalisation — see `test_l0_prompt_matches_e1_for_all_records`. This is the strongest reproducibility guarantee achievable without re-fetching from the upstream feed (explicitly out of scope per `planning/substrate.md`).

## Tests

`tests/test_l0_baseline.py` — 18 tests:

- `test_load_cached_records_returns_283_records` — corpus size lock
- `test_load_cached_records_is_ocid_ascending` — deterministic order
- `test_load_cached_records_is_deterministic_across_calls` — two-call repeatability
- `test_load_cached_records_provenance_envelope_intact` — substrate-honesty envelope
- `test_load_cached_records_carries_e1_reference_fields` — comparator-input fields populated
- `test_load_cached_records_no_network_calls_made` — `requests.get`, `requests.post`, `requests.Session.get` asserted untouched
- `test_missing_archive_raises_substrate_cache_error` — fail-loud contract

## Summary

Makes the `Cue | Lyric | Show` editor-mode switcher achromatic, using a per-mode SF Symbol instead of a colored tint. Leaf 5 of the Quiet Pro epic.

Closes #351

## Motivation

ADR-023 gave the switcher blue/purple/gray tints for at-a-glance mode reading. Quiet Pro's core rule is that cue-type color is the *only* chroma on screen — so the most prominent piece of chrome cannot carry three competing colors. This amends ADR-023: the at-a-glance signal moves from hue to shape.

## Implementation

- `EditorMode` gains a `symbolName` property — a distinct SF Symbol per mode; Show mode's is a lock, reinforcing its read-only nature.
- `EditorModeSwitcher` is rewritten: the active segment uses the achromatic `ink` / `inkOn` treatment (like every other selected control); each segment shows its leading symbol; spacing, radius, and color come from `DS.*`.
- The switcher keeps its accessibility identifiers (`editorModeSwitcher`, `editorModeSegment-<mode>`), so the existing `EditorModeSwitcherUITests` continues to guard the contract.

body:
Refs #1909

## Purpose

- **What does this PR change?** Adds `IMAGE_MEAN` / `IMAGE_STD` constants and applies `(pixels - mean) / std` per channel inside `SigLIPVisionEncoder::forward` (in `candle-binding/src/model_architectures/embedding/multimodal_embedding.rs`) before patch embedding. SigLIP was trained on inputs in `[-1, 1]`, normalized via the per-channel mean/std declared in the model's `preprocessor_config.json` (both 0.5 for SigLIP base and SigLIP2). The Go-side `decodeAndResizeImage` in `semantic-router.go` returns CHW float32 pixels in `[0, 1]`; the prior Rust code consumed those directly, so vision activations sat in the wrong input distribution.
- **Why is this change needed?** On an apples-to-apples passport probe against multi-modal-embed-small (same real-photographic fixture measured both by candle-binding and by the Python production-path pipeline), normalization closes roughly 74% of the residual drift between candle-binding and the Python reference encoder (2.9% drift down to 0.8% drift on the top anchor). Normalization is therefore a correctness fix, not a polish item.
- **Why now / why with PR #1927?** This is the sister to PR #1927, which fixes the SigLIP attentional probe pooling head. PR #1927 fixes the pooling path; this PR fixes the preprocessing path. Together they bring `SigLIPVisionEncoder` to within 1% of the Python reference on the passport probe, and they together unblock the image-modality pack follow-up work referenced in the merged PR #1896.
- **Which module(s) does this affect?** `Bindings` (only `candle-binding/`).

## Test Plan

- Build candle-binding from `candle-binding/`:
  - `cargo build --release --no-default-features --features accelerate`
- Run the normalization-constants unit test:
  - `cargo test --release --no-default-features --features accelerate --lib model_architectures::embedding::multimodal_embedding::tests::test_siglip_image_normalization_constants`
- Run the rest of the existing non-`#[ignore]` tests in the same module to confirm no regression:
  - `cargo test --release --no-default-features --features accelerate --lib model_architectures::embedding::multimodal_embedding`
- For end-to-end empirical verification, reviewers can use the verification branch pinned to commit `8a7e990a596152ec0022c4975b828a737a86d80a`. The receipt directory is at `https://github.com/shraderdm/semantic-router/tree/8a7e990a596152ec0022c4975b828a737a86d80a/docs/probe-2026-05-20-calibration` and contains the apples-to-apples passport-probe artifacts: candle-binding pre-norm and post-norm CSVs, the Python reference CSV, and the probe script that reproduces the Python reference. The same commit also carries both the pooling-head fix (PR #1927's content) and the normalization fix (this PR's content) layered on top.

## Test Result

- `cargo build --release --no-default-features --features accelerate`: succeeds in ~1m16s on M2. The build emits pre-existing crate-wide warnings (unused imports, `unexpected cfg condition value: metal`, `rand::thread_rng` / `rand::Rng::gen` deprecations) but no new warnings introduced by this PR's diff.
- `cargo test ... test_siglip_image_normalization_constants`: passes. The test builds a known `[0, 1]` input tensor, applies `(x - IMAGE_MEAN) / IMAGE_STD` with the same `broadcast_sub` / `broadcast_div` pattern as `SigLIPVisionEncoder::forward`, and asserts each element maps to the expected `[-1, 1]` value within `1e-6`.
- `cargo test ... model_architectures::embedding::multimodal_embedding`: 4 passed, 0 failed, 32 ignored (model-file-dependent integration tests).
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.

**Apples-to-apples passport probe vs Python reference**:

All three rows below measure cosine on the same `inrule_identifier_passport.jpg` fixture (a public-domain Taiwan MOFA passport specimen sourced from Wikipedia; placeholder data, no real identity depicted) against the same `"photograph of a passport page"` anchor text. The candle-binding rows reflect the post-pooling-fix encoder (PR #1927's content) with and without this PR's normalization fix. The Python reference reproduces the production-path multi-modal-embed-small pipeline directly via HuggingFace `transformers` (SigLIP-base-patch16-512 vision_model.pooler_output -> trained Linear(768->384) projection -> L2-normalize for images; MiniLM-L6 mean-pool -> L2-normalize for text).

| Encoder state | Cosine on real passport fixture | Drift from Python reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Post-pooling-fix, pre-norm | 0.6843 | 2.9% |
| Post-pooling-fix, post-norm (this PR) | 0.6991 | 0.8% |
| Python reference (production-path pipeline) | 0.7044 | (baseline) |

Normalization closes roughly 74% of the residual drift between candle-binding and the Python reference encoder.

All three values are backed by committed receipts on the verification branch under `docs/probe-2026-05-20-calibration/`: the candle-binding pre-norm and post-norm cosines live in `calibration_2026_05_20_{prenorm,postnorm}_full.csv`; the Python reference cosine lives in `mmes_2026_05_21_full.csv`; the probe script that produced the Python reference (`probe_mmes_20img.py`) is committed alongside. The directory's `README.md` documents the methodology and provides example `awk` queries that return each row from the corresponding CSV directly.

**Follow-up risks / gaps**: none for the normalization fix itself. The sparse-pack rule definitions, anchor lists, and per-deployment threshold tuning are out of scope here and will land as follow-up work to the merged #1896 sparse-pack.

## Summary

Locks in the P1 atomic-write migration (PRs #17, #18, #19, #20) with a **grep-based CI check** that fails on any new bare `fs.writeFileSync` / `fs.renameSync` / `fs.appendFileSync` / `fs.promises.{writeFile,rename,appendFile}` in production code paths. Every artifact write must go through the durable primitives in `@autoresearch/shared`.

**Net: 9 files, +246/-24.** Includes 1 new file (`scripts/check-atomic-write-anti-drift.mjs`).

## New script: `scripts/check-atomic-write-anti-drift.mjs`

- Scans `packages/*/src` for forbidden patterns

## 8 newly-migrated sites (found by the script)

| File:Line | Migration |
|-----------|-----------|
| `arxiv-mcp/source/paperContent.ts:171` | `renameSync(tempPath, texPath)` → `commitStagedDurable` |
| `hepdata-mcp/tools/registry.ts:131-132` | tmp+writeFileSync+renameSync → `writeBytesAtomicDurable` (drops manual tmp cleanup) |
| `openalex-mcp/api/client.ts:222-225` | local gold-standard rename+dir-fsync → `commitStagedDurable` (dedup) |
| `openalex-mcp/api/contentDownload.ts:159-162` | same shape → `commitStagedDurable` |
| `pdg-mcp/artifacts.ts:61,92` | JSON + JSONL artifact writes → `writeBytesAtomicDurable` |
| `zotero-mcp/zotero/tools.ts:542` | attachment bytes write → `writeBytesAtomicDurable` |

Dropped now-unused `fs` imports in `hepdata-mcp/registry.ts` and `pdg-mcp/artifacts.ts`.

## Smoke-verified

- ✅ Passes on current main (after the 8 sweep migrations)
- ✅ Catches deliberate offender — injected `fs.writeFileSync(...)` into `packages/orchestrator/src/_anti_drift_smoke.ts` → script exits 1 with the offending line + remediation pointer
- ✅ Passes again after offender removed

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm -r build` — green (all packages, including all 5 migrated provider packages)
- [x] `pnpm -r test` — green (1657+ tests across all packages: 519 orchestrator + 708 hep-mcp + 266 shared + 88 arxiv-mcp + 114 openalex-mcp + 42 pdg-mcp + 21 zotero-mcp + 24 hepdata-mcp + ...)
- [x] `pnpm check:atomic-write-anti-drift` — exits 0 with the green message

## End state

With this PR, **the P1 atomic-write durability contract is locked in across the entire monorepo**. Any future code that tries to reintroduce a bare unsafe write will fail CI with a clear remediation pointer. New legitimate exceptions require an explicit allowlist entry with justification.

## Summary

This PR migrates the user-facing documentation from the pantavisor.io website repository into `meta-pantavisor`, making the docs live alongside the code they describe.

**Why this move?**

- **Versioning**: docs now travel with the layer — a tag or release branch captures both the code and its documentation at the same point in time
- **Accuracy**: keeping docs in the same repo as the recipes, KAS configs, and test plans makes it easier to catch and fix drift between what the code does and what the docs say
- **Single source of truth**: contributors can update docs and code in the same PR; reviewers see both changes together

## What's included

All pages from the `learn/` section of pantavisor.io, covering:

- **Concepts** — what Pantavisor is, LXC architecture, device state model, OTA updates, security features
- **Device Setup / Applications** — full application lifecycle: install (pvr CLI, pvtx, Pantahub), configure, view, access, remove
- **Device Setup / Device Access** — serial console, local network (SSH + pvtx UI), Pantahub remote management
- **Porting** — platform YAML, machine YAML, KAS build and flash workflow
- **Troubleshooting** — common issue categories, quick diagnostics, FAQ

## Content changes (vs. original pantavisor.io source)

Beyond the structural move, the imported docs were rewritten to accurately reflect the actual project:

- Correct LXC terminology throughout (not generic "lightweight containers")
- Accurate pvr commands (`pvr deploy trails/0 .` replacing invented `pvr post -a`, `pvr checkout`, etc.)
- Full `pvcontrol` sub-command reference (`container ls`, `daemons ls`, `graph ls`, `buildinfo`)
- Correct log paths (`/run/pantavisor/pv/logs/0/<container>/lxc/`)
- `pvflasher` added as the recommended flashing tool alongside `dd`
- `PANTAVISOR_FEATURES :append` pitfall documented in FAQ and porting guide
- `machines.json` + `makeworkflows` step added to the porting guide
- Broken placeholder links and incomplete sentences fixed

body:
## Summary

Adds `scripts/update-jwks.ts` so the new archive can take over JWK refresh from the old archive's background worker on Render. Part of the [REG-699](https://linear.app/zk-email/issue/REG-699) perf initiative; closes [REG-702](https://linear.app/zk-email/issue/REG-702).

## Why

The old `archive.zk.email background worker` on Render is a long-running Node process whose only job is to call `updateJWKeySet()` every 5 minutes via `node-cron` (see `archive.zk.email/src/util/cron.ts`). The new archive already has `updateJWKeySet()` in `src/lib/db.ts` but nothing calling it on a schedule, so the moment we suspend the old worker (REG-703) the `JsonWebKeySets` table stops being updated.

This PR closes that gap.

## Approach

- Standalone one-shot script (not a long-running service) so it can run as a Render Cron Job instead of a `$7/mo` always-on background worker. Render Cron Jobs are billed by runtime; 1.1s every 5 minutes is essentially free.
- `tsx` added as a devDep so the script can use `@/` path aliases consistent with the rest of the codebase. The existing `generate-api-key.ts` predates this and uses `ts-node` with relative imports; new scripts should use this pattern.
- Witness.co integration intentionally **not** ported. Team confirmed Witness is deprecated and nothing downstream consumes the on-chain witnesses. The leftover frontend markers are tracked in [REG-704](https://linear.app/zk-email/issue/REG-704) (PR #27).
- Script exits 1 if `updateJWKeySet()` returns no result so Render flags the run as failed (alertable). On success it logs the row id + lastUpdated for traceability.

## Tested

Ran locally against prod-duplicate (the DB backing `archive-new`):

\`\`\`
$ pnpm jwks:update
[2026-05-21T15:28:40.564Z] starting JWK refresh
[2026-05-21T15:28:41.648Z] JWK refresh OK (row id=49, lastUpdated=2026-05-21T15:28:41.488Z)
\`\`\`

End-to-end runtime: ~1.1s. A new row was inserted (id=49) because Google had rotated their x509 cert since the last entry on December 2 (id=48) — illustrating that the JsonWebKeySets table had been stale for nearly six months without the background worker running. Once this cron is live, the table stays current with a 5-min cadence again.

## Render Cron Job setup (next step, manual via dashboard)

These steps need to be done in the Render dashboard before old archive's background worker can be decommissioned (REG-703). Documented in the script header too:

1. **New** → **Cron Job**
2. **Repository**: \`zkemail/archive\`, branch \`develop\` (or \`main\` after merge)
3. **Region**: same as \`archive-new\` web service (probably Oregon/Frankfurt — match it)
4. **Schedule**: \`*/5 * * * *\`
5. **Build command**: \`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm prisma generate\`
6. **Run command**: \`pnpm jwks:update\`
7. **Environment variables**: \`DATABASE_URL\` (same value as \`archive-new\`)
8. **Plan**: Starter

After it's been live for ~10 minutes, verify a fresh \`lastUpdated\` timestamp on the latest \`JsonWebKeySets\` row.

## Test plan

- [x] CI lint/build/typecheck green
- [x] After merge: provision the Render Cron Job per the steps above — `archive-new-jwks-cron` (`crn-d881iom7r5hc73f679p0`) exists and is running on the \`*/5 * * * *\` schedule
- [x] Wait 5–10 minutes, then check `JsonWebKeySets` in DB: latest `lastUpdated` advances every 5 minutes — verified: row id=241 lastUpdated 2026-06-04 18:35:59, row id=240 at 18:26:02 (and so on at every 5-min interval)
- [x] Confirm `pg_stat_activity` shows incoming connections from a new Render service IP every 5 minutes — verified during cron execution windows; cron runs to completion in <1s and connections are transient

## Follow-ups

- REG-703: decommission old `archive.zk.email` web service + background worker once this cron has been live for a week with no missed runs

Tasks are grouped by category on the Focus page and can be filtered by category on the All page. Categories sync to Supabase and integrate with the existing local-first architecture.

- **New `Category` type** (`src/lib/types.ts`): id, name, color, sortOrder, timestamps, and soft-delete support

- **Settings page** (`src/routes/settings/+page.svelte`): full UI for managing categories—create with color picker, inline edit/delete, drag-to-reorder with up/down buttons

- **Database schema** (`supabase/migrations/20260521120000_categories.sql`): `categories` table with user_id FK, RLS policies, indexes, and `category_id` FK on tasks with ON DELETE SET NULL
- **Sync integration** (`src/lib/sync.svelte.ts`, `src/lib/sync-helpers.ts`): categories pushed/pulled in fullSync and Realtime, with `categoryToRow`/`rowToCategory` converters; categories synced before tasks to avoid FK dangling
- **Store** (`src/lib/store.svelte.ts`): new `categoryStore` and `reloadCategories()` function; `reloadAll()` helper for coordinated reloads

- Categories use a predefined color palette (`CATEGORY_COLORS`) with CSS custom properties
- Sort order is auto-assigned on creation (max existing + 1) and swapped on reorder
- Dangling `categoryId` references (from soft-deletes on other devices) gracefully fall back to Uncategorized in the UI

## a21-test-stripe-subscription-webhook-paths

`src/payments/webhook_dispatcher.rs` has two handlers — `handle_invoice_paid` and `handle_invoice_payment_failed` — that are the entire billing flow for Stripe-subscription members. Every time a Stripe-managed subscription successfully bills, `invoice.paid` fires and `handle_invoice_paid` extends the member's `dues_paid_until`. Every time a charge fails, `invoice.payment_failed` fires and `handle_invoice_payment_failed` triggers `notify_subscription_payment_failed` (which emails the member and dispatches `AdminAlert`).

Neither handler has a test in `tests/stripe_webhook_test.rs`. The file covers `payment_intent.succeeded`, `charge.refunded`, `subscription.deleted`, `checkout.session.completed` — but invoice events are conspicuously absent. The architectural review missed this; an audit during deployment planning surfaced it.

This matters for the upcoming neontemple.com production migration: every imported member starts in `StripeSubscription` mode and stays there until they organically migrate. The `invoice.paid` and `invoice.payment_failed` handlers will fire for every renewal cycle of every imported member. Going to production without test coverage on the code path 100% of paying members exercise is a real risk.

2. Seeds a row for every existing org: prefix `MFG-`, pad_width 5, yearly reset (matches chassis defaults).

4. Backfills any `manufacturing_runs.run_number IS NULL` rows in chronological order per org.

**Handler (`supabase/functions/manufacturing-api/index.ts`):**
- Imports `nextDocNumber` from `_shared/numbering.ts`.

## Summary

The zero billing checkout route (`turbo/apps/api/src/signals/routes/zero-billing-checkout.ts`) pinned `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` to `VM0_WEB_URL`, but the **"Upgrade plan"** button lives in the **platform** app (`apps/platform`). `startCheckout$` builds those URLs from `window.location.href`, so their origin is always the platform app origin — i.e. `APP_URL`, not `VM0_WEB_URL`.

`APP_URL` never equals `VM0_WEB_URL` in any environment (test stub `:3002` vs `:3001`, local dev `app.vm7.ai` vs `www.vm7.ai`, prod `app.vm0.ai` vs `www.vm0.ai`), so the origin check rejected every request with `400 successUrl and cancelUrl must match the platform origin`.

The wrong variable was written when the API checkout route was created (#12596/#12606, 2026-05-11) but stayed dormant — the platform still hit the old `apps/web` checkout route. PR #14136 (2026-05-20) deleted that web route and proxied checkout traffic to this API route, activating the latent bug and breaking "Upgrade plan" everywhere.

## Changes

- `zero-billing-checkout.ts`: validate against `env("APP_URL")` instead of `env("VM0_WEB_URL")`, matching the sibling `zero-billing-redeem.ts` and `zero-billing-portal.ts` routes which already use `APP_URL`.
- `zero-billing-checkout.test.ts`: the test masked the bug — its `APP_ORIGIN` constant was set to `http://localhost:3001` (the env-stub's `VM0_WEB_URL`, not `APP_URL` which is `:3002`). Corrected the constant and the test title.

No workflow or Vercel env changes needed: the shared `.github/actions/web-api-env` action already injects `APP_URL` unconditionally for the API project in both preview and production deploys.

This PR executes a global aesthetic and structural overhaul of the service page matrix to align with the premium brand identity established in `corporate-yoga-day-bangalore.html`.

Key Changes:
- **Structural Overhaul**: Applied a unified premium layout (#F8F5F0 background, #333333 typography, 80px container padding) to core service pages: `Online-Yoga-Classes.html`, `Online-Personal-Training-classes.html`, and `Online-Pranayama-Classes.html`.
- **Legacy Redirect Transformation**: Converted all legacy form-only links into dedicated standalone landing pages for Postpartum Yoga, Kids Yoga, Hatha & Vinyasa, Senior Yoga, and PCOD Yoga.
- **Infinite Marquee Component**: Replaced static service rows with a high-performance, pure-CSS horizontal marquee across all core pages. This component features seamless looping, automatic translation, and mobile-responsive card sizing (350px).
- **Instructor Credential Alignment**: Hardwired Anusha's teaching metric to "1,500+ teaching and clinical corporate wellness hours taught" across the entire repository.
- **SEO Internal Linking**: Integrated strategic internal links within new service pages back to high-performing blog assets (Back Pain Relief, Sleep Yoga) to strengthen keyword anchoring.
- **Responsive Optimization**: Standardized padding and font behaviors for mobile (<=480px), tablet, and desktop breakpoints to ensure a perfect fluid scale without horizontal scroll.

Verification:
- Performed thorough audits using Playwright to verify unique marquee containers, clickable service cards, and visual layout stability on mobile.
- Verified absence of duplicate markup and ensured HTML validity across all modified files.
- Cleaned up all temporary verification scripts and artifacts before submission.
